# Third-party code used by the tests

| Directory | What | Origin |
|---|---|---|
| `engine/` | message coding (`msg.c`, `huffman*.c`) for the demo reader; collision (`cm_*.c`), `q_shared`, `q_math`, `md4` | oDFe (a quake3e fork), `code/qcommon`, commit `93e6d6be25041064f10be6e21e639dbf4dbc060c`; GPL-2.0-or-later (id Software) |
| `engine_shim/` | `sv_world.c` (entity clipping, verbatim from oDFe `code/server/sv_world.c` of the same commit) with a shim `server.h` that supplies only what it needs | oDFe, GPL-2.0-or-later |
| `engine_f32/` | `cm_trace.c`, `cm_patch.c`, `cm_polylib.c` of `engine/` with floats where oDFe has doubles, generated by `make_f32.sh` (the ioq3 form of the code) | derived from the files above |
| `miniz/` | deflate for the golden files (default; `cmake -DDFG_ZLIB=ON` or `DFG_ZLIB=1 build.sh` use the system zlib instead, same stream format) | miniz 3.0.2 (https://github.com/richgel999/miniz), MIT, `LICENSE` in the directory |

The files are copies, not modified (except the shim). To update the engine copy, take the same files from a newer oDFe
and remake and re-test the golden files: a change in the collision code can change what the replay sees.

## Why the collision code exists three times

A recording only replays bit for bit with the collision arithmetic of the engine that made it. The last bit of a trace's end point
differs between engines, and a player sliding along a wall at 2500 units/s shows that within a few steps:

| copy | what it is | used for recordings of |
|---|---|---|
| plain | oDFe / quake3e: doubles in the brush, tree and patch code, SSE | the 64 bit builds of iDFe, `Q3 1.32e`, ... |
| `_x87` | the same, compiled with `-mfpmath=387` | 32 bit x86 builds of those engines (e.g. `iDFe ... win_mingw-x86`) |
| `_f32` | `engine_f32/`: floats instead of doubles | the ioq3 based DeFRaG engines (`iodfe ...`) |

`engine_shim/coll_names.h` gives every global of `cm_*.c` and `sv_world.c` a suffix when they are compiled again (`COLL_SUFFIX`), and
`host/coll.h` calls the copy the golden file asks for (`GOLD_KNOWN_X87` / `GOLD_KNOWN_F32` in its `knownFlags`, chosen by
`dfgolden make` from the engine version in the recording).
